index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents an organizational structure of the calibration process for black-box large language models (LLMs), depicted as a hierarchical flowchart. The global layout is a tree-like diagram with a vertical main axis on the left labeled 'Calibration Process for Black-Box LLMs' in a light brown rectangular box. From this axis, two primary branches extend horizontally to the right: one leading to a central brown oval node titled 'Confidence Calibration Methods for Black-Box LLMs', and the other to a teal oval node labeled 'Applications'.

The 'Confidence Calibration Methods for Black-Box LLMs' node branches into two main categories: 'Confidence Elicitation Methods' and 'Calibration Methods', both represented as rounded orange rectangles. 'Confidence Elicitation Methods' further splits into three subcategories: 'Consistency Methods', 'Self-Reflections Methods', and 'Hybrid Methods', each also in rounded orange rectangles. These subcategories branch into more specific techniques: 'Consistency Methods' includes 'Similar Based Methods' and 'Entropy Based Methods'; 'Self-Reflections Methods' includes 'Direct Reflection Based Methods' and 'Response Optimization Methods'; and 'Hybrid Methods' includes 'Post-Processing Combined Based Methods' and 'Third-Party Proxy Based Methods'. Each of these specific methods is shown in a lighter orange rounded rectangle.

The 'Calibration Methods' category branches into two subcategories: 'Calibration Methods' and 'Calibration Measurement Methods', both in rounded orange rectangles. 'Calibration Methods' further divides into 'Post-Processing Based Methods' and 'Third-Party Proxy Based Methods', while 'Calibration Measurement Methods' splits into 'Error-Based Methods' and 'Correlation-Based Methods', all in lighter orange rounded rectangles.

Each of these specific method types is connected via horizontal lines to a gray rectangular box on the far right, which lists representative academic references (e.g., 'Manakul et al., (2023)', 'Zhang et al. (2024b)', etc.) associated with that method.

The 'Applications' node branches into two subcategories: 'Risk Assessment and Mitigation' and 'User-interactive Mode Optimization', both in rounded teal rectangles. These are similarly linked to gray rectangular boxes listing relevant references (e.g., 'Qin et al. (2024)', 'Steyvers et al. (2024)').

All connections between nodes are represented by solid black lines, indicating hierarchical or categorical relationships. The color coding distinguishes major categories (brown for main topic, orange for calibration methods, teal for applications), while the gray boxes serve as reference anchors. The diagram uses consistent shapes—ovals for main categories, rounded rectangles for subcategories and methods, and plain rectangles for references—to maintain visual clarity and logical flow.
